title: High-pressure phase transitions in the quantum spin liquid candidate Na2Co2TeO6 probed by Raman spectroscopy
authors: Ihsan Ahmed Kolasseri, Maria Mei Ravnebæk, Subhadip Das, Carl Jonas Linnemann, Haidong Zhou, Christian Frydendahl, Martin Bremholm, Yong P. Chen
abstract: The quasi-2D magnet Na2Co2TeO6 (NCTO) is a candidate for a Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquid (KQSL) state. Pressure-tuning in such materials is of interest as a potential method to tune the Kitaev exchange interactions, which are strongly dependent on bond geometry. Here we report a Raman spectroscopic study of NCTO inside a diamond anvil cell (DAC) with pressure applied up to 16.3 GPa. Based on the changes in the Raman modes, this pressure range is divided into three regions. The appearance and disappearance of several modes and changes in the polarization dependence of the representative modes, most prominently above 13.8 GPa, point to pressure-induced phase transitions in this material.
summary: This work uses high-pressure Raman spectroscopy on $	ext{Na}_2	ext{Co}_2	ext{TeO}_6$ to study its behavior as a candidate Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquid. By monitoring changes in vibrational modes up to 16.3 GPa, the researchers identified multiple pressure-induced phase transitions. These findings provide experimental evidence for tuning the quantum magnetic interactions in this strongly correlated material.
main_problem: The study investigates pressure-induced phase transitions in $	ext{Na}_2	ext{Co}_2	ext{TeO}_6$, a material candidate for a Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquid (KQSL) state.
main_result: Raman spectroscopy reveals that the material undergoes structural phase transitions at high pressures, notably marked by the emergence of a new Raman mode ($	ext{L}_1$) above 13.8 GPa.
method: The research employed Raman spectroscopy performed inside a Diamond Anvil Cell (DAC) to probe the material's vibrational modes under extreme pressure.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Na}_2	ext{Co}_2	ext{TeO}_6$, a quasi-2D magnet whose magnetic interactions are hypothesized to be governed by the Kitaev model due to strong spin-orbit coupling in the $	ext{Co}^{2+}$ ions.
key_observables: Changes in Raman mode frequencies, appearance/disappearance of modes, and changes in the polarization dependence of representative modes.
important_parameters: Applied pressure up to 16.3 GPa (and up to 20 GPa in related studies); the pressure evolution is analyzed in Low, Medium, and High Pressure regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that changes in Raman modes are indicative of underlying structural or electronic phase transitions, and that the Kitaev model is relevant for describing the magnetic interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic crystal structure, ambient pressure spectra, and waterfall plots showing the evolution of various Raman modes across the applied pressure range, highlighting mode changes at high pressure.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Raman spectra across different pressure regimes (LP, MP, HP), correlating observed spectroscopic changes (mode shifts, new peaks) with potential structural phase transitions in the KQSL candidate.
why_interesting: The study uses high-pressure spectroscopy to probe the fundamental electronic and structural transitions in a material relevant to exotic quantum magnetism (Kitaev model), providing experimental data on tuning quantum ground states.
